Definition: properly, to grate, i.e. (figuratively) to anger
BiblicalUsage: Garah means to grate, to stir up, to meddle — and it is the word for picking a fight. Amaziah is warned not to meddle to his hurt in 2 Kings 14:10, and the same warning stands in 2 Chronicles 25:19. The sons of the king of the north shall be stirred up in Daniel 11:10, and Israel is told not to meddle with the children of Ammon in Deuteronomy 2:19.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe meddling is the road to a fall. Amaziah was told to stay home, and he went out and fell, and I hold that the fights God tells us not to pick are the ones that would destroy us.
